content.title: Masters champion's son is banned from Augusta after 'ruining' special moment
content.text: Some of Gary Player's fondest golfing memories are at the Augusta National, but the same can't be said for his son, Wayne.Sporting great Player is a three-time Masters winner, and has kicked off the tournament each year since 2012 as part of their honorary starters ceremony.5Gary Player is set to tee off the 2026 Masters for the 14th year in a rowCredit: GettyThis will be no different in the 2026 edition, with the South African once again set to join fellow icons Jack Nicklaus, and Tom Watson in hitting the ceremonial first tee shots of the major on Thursday.And it's fair to say Player will be hoping that his role in the upcoming annual tradition will be less eventful than in previous years.OvershadowedFive years ago, the 2021 Honorary Starters ceremony was marred by a controversial incident involving Player's son, Wayne.In a special edition of the ceremonial event, the first-ever black player at the Masters, Lee Elder, joined Nicklaus and Player for the opening shots.However, the poignant moment was soon overshadowed by Wayne, who was serving as his father's caddie in the ceremonial event.Introducing Elder, club chairman Fred Ridley gave a speech to honour the historic former player's legacy.As the cameras panned to Elder, Wayne promptly held up a pack of OnCore golf balls - a brand endorsing his dad Gary.Report AdIn a clear attempt to advertise the brand, fans and Augusta National were quick to notice Wayne's actions, who came down hard on him.The son of the golf icon immediately had his accreditation for the event revoked by the golf club, and was told he would not be allowed to return for future tournaments.'Tacky'A year after the incident, Wayne addressed the incident, and revealed the Augusta National had not changed their stance on his ban.5Wayne Player is one of golf icon Gary's six childrenCredit: Getty5Lee Elder passed away in 2021, months after being honoured at the Masters' Honorary Starters ceremonyCredit: GettySpeaking to Golf Digest in 2022, he reflected: "Well, they say there's no such thing as bad publicity. I found out that that's not quite true."I had probably 50 texts after that, 40 of them said I'm a marketing genius, ten were like, 'What the hell were you thinking?' - It wasn't premeditated, but it was a tacky thing."Player Jr said he had written a letter of apology to club chairman Fred Ridley, where he expressed his love for the tournament.Despite his attempts, he revealed this fell on deaf ears, and remains banned from the famous course in Georgia.On the club's response, Wayne revealed: “It said, 'Thanks, but no thanks.'“It said, 'You know, we appreciate you reaching out and apologising, we accept your apology, but we are not changing our position, we are not going to allow you back.'5The 90th edition of the Masters is nearly upon us, but Wayne Player will not be allowed to attend in personCredit: Getty"'You ruined a special moment in the history of the game of golf.'Wayne also shared that he had reached out to Elder, whose career and achievements were being celebrated while the controversy unfolded.Elder passed away in November 2021, having made history in 1975 as the first black golfer to play in Augusta.Opening up on their conversation, Wayne said: “I've got Lee's cellphone number. I called and I said, ‘You know, Lee, I love you guys.’"You know, everyone said I was disrespectful for a special moment in time for Elder. I said I was sorry, and I didn’t mean to take up his special time. "And he said, ‘Wayne, you know how much I love you. Right?’ It didn’t cross his mind. That’s important for people to know.” 5Gary Player is one of only six golfers to achieve the career Grand SlamCredit: GettyWho is Wayne Player?The third of Gary Player's six children, Wayne once had dreams of following in his father's footsteps.The 68-year-old competed in 17 PGA Tour events in his younger days, but never made a cut.It's fair to say his father's legacy took some beating, with the legendary Player boasting nine major titles across a 19-year period between 1959 and 1978. He won three Open Championships, three Masters, two PGA Championships, and one U.S. Open.Having struggled to live up to this, Wayne has been involved in various health and fitness endeavours following his playing career.
